Jira issues and Confluence pages on the sites the person grants.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Atlassian account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [developer.atlassian.com](https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/)
- **Settings:** `ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_ID`, `ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Added with:** `everyapp provider add --oauth atlassian`

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/atlassian/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `everyapp provider show atlassian` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

Calls go to api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/&lt;cloud id>/… ; the cloud id comes from /oauth/token/accessible-resources.

1. Open [developer.atlassian.com](https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/) and create an OAuth app (sometimes called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Allow the scopes behind the sets your apps use (the table below), and no others.
4. Copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret is often shown once.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Atlassian) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
everyapp provider add --oauth atlassian
everyapp secret set ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_ID ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Atlassian account (who you are) | `read:me` |
| `jira.read` | Jira issues and projects (read) | `read:jira-work`, `read:jira-user` |
| `jira.write` | Jira issues (read and write) | `read:jira-work`, `write:jira-work` |
| `confluence.read` | Confluence pages (read) | `read:confluence-content.all`, `read:confluence-space.summary` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  atlassian: { access: "read", scopes: ["jira.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `everyapp provider show atlassian` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Atlassian**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.
